description: The indirection half of the policy. The real work is grouping the digest by day. Alongside it the change introduces a NotificationSender interface, an EmailSender that wraps the existing sendEmail one-to-one, and a SenderRegistry keyed by string, then replaces the digest's direct sendEmail call with registry.get("email").send(...). After the change there is one implementation, one registered kind, and one caller; a reader of digest.ts now opens sender.ts and email.ts to learn that an email gets sent, and the string key can fail at runtime where the import could not. The day grouping and its comment are must-not-flag.

evidence_trace: src/notify/sender.ts:3 declares NotificationSender; EmailSender at :7-11 is its only implementation and delegates to sendEmail unchanged
src/notify/sender.ts:13 declares SenderRegistry with exactly one registered kind
src/notify/digest.ts:24 is the only caller of the registry in the checkout (grep for SenderRegistry)
digest.ts previously imported sendEmail directly, so the change replaces a one-line import with three layers
finding.failure_scenario: A reader of sendDigest has to open sender.ts and then email.ts to learn that an email is sent, and a typo in the "email" key becomes a runtime throw where the direct import failed at compile time.
finding.model_authored_prose: SenderRegistry (sender.ts:13), NotificationSender, and EmailSender add three layers between sendDigest and sendEmail with one implementation and one caller behind them. Keep the direct sendEmail import until a second sender exists.

prContext.title: notify: group the digest by day and route sends through a sender registry
prContext.description: The daily digest listed every update as its own line, so a busy week ran to seventy lines. It now groups by day. Sending goes through a NotificationSender registry so a second channel can be added later.
